title: Measure masters
goal: I can solve balance puzzles and pouring puzzles. I can change units. I can tell the time to 5 minutes and find how long.

learn.intro: A level balance has the same mass on both sides, so you can swap a thing for what balances it. On a clock the short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. Pour jugs one step at a time.

example.problem: The scale is level. 1 melon balances 3 plums. 1 plum has a mass of 50 g. Find the mass of the melon.
steps: The melon is as heavy as 3 plums.

example2.problem: A lesson starts at 8:50 am and lasts 25 minutes. When does it end?

howto.title: How to start
steps: Balance: both sides are equal. Swap things.
Time: count on to the next hour first.
Jugs: write both amounts after each pour.

facts.title: Units and time
lines: am: midnight to noon. pm: noon to midnight.
The long hand on 7 means 35 minutes.

try.text: One tin balances 4 pens. One pen has a mass of 25 g. Find the mass of the tin. {b} g
try.explanation: The tin is as heavy as 4 pens. 4 × 25 g = 100 g. Check: 25 + 25 + 25 + 25 = 100.

items.text: Read the clocks. Write each time.
items.explanation: The long hand shows the minutes: count in 5s. A: long hand on 7 is 35 minutes, short hand past 4: 4:35. B: long hand on 10 is 50 minutes: 8:50. C: long hand on 3 is 15 minutes: 11:15.

items.text: Write am or pm.
items.explanation: am is from midnight to noon. pm is from noon to midnight. (a) Breakfast is in the morning: am. (b) 1:30 after lunch: pm. (c) Bedtime at night: pm. (d) Sunrise is in the morning: am.

items.text: Find the end or start time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A film begins at 3:40 pm and runs for 35 minutes. It finishes at {b} : {b} pm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A class starts at 9:50 am and ends at 10:30 am. It lasts {b} minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A game ends at 5:05 pm. It lasted 25 minutes. It started at {b} : {b} pm.

items.explanation: (a) 3:40 to 4:00 is 20 minutes. 15 more minutes: 4:15. (b) 9:50 to 10:00 is 10 minutes, and 10:00 to 10:30 is 30 minutes: 40 minutes. (c) Count back 5 minutes to 5:00, then 20 more minutes: 4:40.

items.text: A trip starts at 9:35 am and ends at 11:05 am. How long is the trip?

parts.label: a
parts.text: The trip is {b} hour and {b} minutes long.

items.explanation: 9:35 to 10:00 is 25 minutes. 10:00 to 11:00 is 1 hour. 11:00 to 11:05 is 5 minutes. 25 + 5 = 30 minutes. The trip is 1 hour 30 minutes.

items.text: All the scales are level.
items.explanation: Scale 2: 1 lemon is 50 g. Scale 1: 1 apple is as heavy as 3 lemons: 3 × 50 = 150 g.

items.text: A 5 ℓ jug and an 8 ℓ jug have no marks. Both are empty.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Fill the 8 ℓ jug. Pour into the 5 ℓ jug until it is full. The 8 ℓ jug holds {b} ℓ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Empty the 5 ℓ jug. Pour the 3 ℓ in. It needs {b} ℓ more.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Fill the 8 ℓ jug. Pour into the 5 ℓ jug until it is full. The 8 ℓ jug holds {b} ℓ.

items.explanation: (a) 8 - 5 = 3 ℓ is left in the 8 ℓ jug. (b) The 5 ℓ jug holds 3 ℓ. 5 - 3 = 2 ℓ more fill it. (c) The 8 ℓ jug gives 2 ℓ: 8 - 2 = 6 ℓ is left.

items.text: Circle the better unit.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The mass of a school bag   {circ:g|kg}

items.explanation: An egg is light: grams. A pencil is short: centimetres. A school bag is heavy: kilograms. Water in a jug is measured in litres.

items.text: Lily has a green ribbon 85 cm long. Her yellow ribbon is 27 cm shorter.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The yellow ribbon is {b} cm long.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Lily joins them end to end with an overlap of 4 cm. The long ribbon is {b} cm.

parts.label: c
parts.text: She cuts 3 pieces of 20 cm from the green ribbon. Green ribbon left: {b} cm

items.explanation: (a) 85 - 27 = 58 cm. (b) Together 85 + 58 = 143 cm. The overlap is counted twice, so take away 4 cm: 139 cm. (c) 3 × 20 = 60 cm cut off. 85 - 60 = 25 cm left.

items.text: Change the units.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A bag has 2 kg of rice. Mei uses 750 g. Rice left: {bw} g

items.text: Change the units.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A rope is 5 m. Ali cuts off 130 cm. Rope left: {b} cm

items.text: A bucket holds 12 ℓ. It has 4 ℓ in it. Mei pours in 2 ℓ each time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many pours fill the bucket? {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: After 3 pours the bucket holds {b} ℓ.

items.explanation: (a) The bucket needs 12 - 4 = 8 ℓ more. 8 ÷ 2 = 4 pours. (b) 3 pours add 6 ℓ. 4 + 6 = 10 ℓ.

items.text: 4 plums balance 1 pear. A pear and 2 plums balance 600 g.
items.explanation: Swap the pear for 4 plums. Then 4 plums and 2 plums, which is 6 plums, balance 600 g. 600 ÷ 6 = 100, so 1 plum is 100 g. The pear is 4 plums: 400 g. Check: 400 + 100 + 100 = 600.
items.hint: Swap the pear for 4 plums. How many plums are on that side?

items.text: A 5 ℓ jug and a 7 ℓ jug have no marks. Get exactly 4 ℓ. Three steps are done.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After step 5 the jugs hold {b} ℓ and {b} ℓ.

parts.label: b
parts.text: At the end the 7 ℓ jug holds {b} ℓ.

items.explanation: Step 4: pour the 2 ℓ into the 5 ℓ jug (2, 0). Step 5: fill the 7 ℓ jug (2, 7). Step 6: pour from the 7 ℓ jug into the 5 ℓ jug until it is full. It needs 3 ℓ more, so 7 - 3 = 4 ℓ is left (5, 4). The 7 ℓ jug holds 4 ℓ.
items.hint: Pour the 2 ℓ into the 5 ℓ jug. Then fill the 7 ℓ jug.

items.text: A museum tour has 4 stops. Each stop takes 20 minutes. There is a 5-minute walk between stops. The tour starts at 9:15 am.
items.explanation: 4 stops of 20 minutes is 80 minutes. There are only 3 walks between 4 stops: 3 × 5 = 15 minutes. 80 + 15 = 95 minutes. 9:15 plus 95 minutes: 9:15 to 10:15 is 60 minutes, then 35 more: 10:50 am.

items.text: The 24-hour clock. After noon add 12 to the hour: 1:30 pm is 13:30.
items.hint: After noon: add 12 to the hour. Going back: take 12 away.

items.text: Scale 1: 1 box and 2 cups balance 4 cups. Scale 2: 1 box and 1 cup balance 600 g.
items.explanation: Scale 1: take 2 cups off both sides. 1 box balances 2 cups. Scale 2: swap the box for 2 cups: 3 cups balance 600 g, so a cup is 200 g. The box is 2 cups: 400 g. Check scale 1: 400 + 200 + 200 = 800 = 4 × 200.
items.hint: Take 2 cups off both sides of scale 1.

items.text: Make your own balance puzzle with apples and lemons. One apple must be 200 g. Many answers are right.

answer.text: Open. Example: Scale 1: 1 apple balances 4 lemons. Scale 2: 1 lemon balances a 50 g weight. Then 1 apple is 4 × 50 = 200 g.

items.explanation: Example: a lemon is 50 g and an apple is 4 lemons, so the apple is 200 g. Another way: 1 apple balances a 200 g weight, with a second scale for a lemon.
items.hint: Start from 200 g. What balances it?

items.text: A clock gains 3 minutes every hour. It is set right at 7:00 am.

parts.label: a
parts.text: At 11:00 am the clock shows {b} : {b} am.

parts.label: b
parts.text: It shows 12:15 pm. The right time is {b} : {b}.

items.explanation: (a) 7 am to 11 am is 4 hours: 4 × 3 = 12 minutes fast, 11:12 am. (b) At the right time 12:00 pm the clock is 5 × 3 = 15 minutes fast, so it shows 12:15 pm.
items.hint: How many hours have passed? 3 minutes each hour.

items.text: A show begins at 6:50 pm and runs for 35 minutes. It finishes at {b} : {b} pm.
items.explanation: 6:50 to 7:00 is 10 minutes. 25 more minutes: 7:25 pm.

items.text: 2 kg 300 g = {bw} g
1 melon balances 3 pears. 1 pear is 200 g. The melon is {b} g.
items.explanation: 3 pears: 3 × 200 = 600 g. The melon is 600 g.
